title: Introduction to Psychological Testing: Definition, Nature and Characteristics
summary: Meaning of psychological test; nature and characteristics of tests; test as a measuring instrument; uses of psychological testing.
objectives: List characteristics of a good test.
revision: Psychological test = standardised measure of behaviour. Four pillars: Standardisation, Reliability, Validity, Norms.
traps: Standardisation means uniform administration and scoring.
A test must be both reliable and valid to be useful.
confusions: Confusing a test with a questionnaire.
Believing a test must always produce a numerical score.

notes.t: A standardised measure of a sample of behaviour. A psychological test is a standardised procedure for sampling behaviour and describing it with scores or categories.

A psychological test is a standardised instrument designed to measure one or more aspects of human behaviour, such as intelligence, personality, aptitude, attitude or achievement. It provides a systematic way to observe and describe behaviour.

notes.c: Characteristics of a good psychological test
r: Uniform procedures for administration and scoring.
Consistency of test scores over time and across forms.
The test measures what it claims to measure.
Reference scores for interpreting individual performance.
Feasible to administer, score and interpret.

notes.t: A psychological test is a standardised measure of behaviour. Standardisation, reliability, validity and norms are the four pillars of good testing frequently tested in UGC NET.

mnemonics.title: SRVN
mnemonics.text: S — Standardisation, R — Reliability, V — Validity, N — Norms
